sections.label: Our Teams

briefs.headline: Chelsea outgun Brighton 4-3 in a seven-goal thriller
briefs.summary: Lavia, Neto and Joao Pedro had Chelsea three up inside 32 minutes Sunday, and Cole Palmer answered in the 74th after a Yalcouye strike and an own goal closed it to one; Gross headed Brighton's third in stoppage time.

briefs.headline: Reds take the rubber game 7-5 at Wrigley
briefs.summary: Sal Stewart's 31st homer and Hector Rodriguez's three-run drive backed Chase Burns' seven-strikeout start Sunday; Pete Crow-Armstrong homered twice more to reach 38.

briefs.headline: Pirates hold off the Cardinals 5-4 for the series
briefs.summary: Esmerlyn Valdez's two-run homer and Jared Triolo's solo shot built a 4-0 lead Sunday and Braxton Ashcraft took his 14th win; St. Louis' comeback fell a run short and Pittsburgh took two of three.

briefs.headline: Crew concede three unanswered in 3-1 home loss
briefs.summary: Brais Mendez put Columbus up in the eighth minute Sunday, but Polster, Turgeman and Gil answered by the 79th; New England has won five times this season after conceding first, most in MLS.

briefs.headline: Wimes' 86th-minute winner keeps No. 7 WVU perfect
briefs.summary: Kansas transfer Saige Wimes' first Mountaineer goal, with just over four minutes left, beat Army 2-1 at West Point Sunday after Bella Conti had tied it; the women are 4-0.

briefs.headline: Browns keep three quarterbacks on the initial 53
briefs.summary: Deshaun Watson starts with Shedeur Sanders behind him and Taylen Green third; Dillon Gabriel went to injured reserve, designated for return, among 20 moves announced Sunday.

briefs.headline: Bengals cut to 53 with Burrow and Flacco atop the depth chart
briefs.summary: Cincinnati terminated four contracts and waived 30 players Sunday, with Ja'Sir Taylor and Brian Parker to injury lists; six receivers made it behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Waivers clear at 1 p.m. ET today.

sections.label: Around the Leagues

briefs.headline: Banzuke day delivers the autumn rankings, and a sold-out Aki
briefs.summary: The JSA published the new banzuke Monday: Onosato at east yokozuna, Hoshoryu at west, with Kirishima, Kotozakura and Aonishiki at ozeki, and every Tokyo session already sold out. Its English pages still post no schedule, so the derived Sept. 13 opening, 13 days out, remains formally unconfirmed.

sections.note: r/Sumo was unreachable a ninth straight morning; the sweep ran on the JSA's pages and news searches. Hoshoryu's readiness is the question the rankings do not answer.

sections.label: In Season

coming_in.item: Opens TOMORROW in joint and coastal waters: one fish per day, 15-inch minimum, with mandatory harvest reporting - reconfirmed on the division's pages this morning. The bag-limit table itself still shows last year's closure, so go by the season notice, not the table.
The youth weekend runs Saturday and Sunday, daily bag 6, possession 12; the general season follows Sept. 12 and runs to Feb. 28.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

prime.item: Coastal waters: an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one per day; unlawful to possess a fish over 27 inches.
Coastal waters: a 14-to-20-inch slot, three per day, of which one may exceed 26 inches.

going_out.item: The first gun window, in SELECTED COUNTIES only, closes a week from today - the county list is not in the pamphlet's summary table, so none is named here. Daily 1, season limit 2; electronic registration required.
going_out.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

sections.note: The DNR's separate migratory bird summary is still untranscribed in this repo, so no dove or goose date prints. WV trout stocking is a January-May program; the summer search stays silent, as expected.

waters.working: Less than half of yesterday's 300 and dropping fast - the weekend's color is leaving and the river is settling into low, clear late-summer form. That is a long-leader game: a dry-dropper with the dry doing the work, terrestrials tight to the banks as the morning warms, and the softer tailouts before the sun gets on them.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.1 ft - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Holding at pool - shad are the forage, so a white swimbait across the wing-dam seams early, then slow a jig down the same edges as the sun climbs.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.7 ft and falling - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Easing off below the dam - a crawfish crankbait ticked along the riprap and lock wall, and a jig worked the barge cuts for fish sitting off the current.

waters.reading: Sound high 11:15 AM at 3.9 ft and 11:30 PM at 3.6 ft at Hampstead; lows 5:15 AM at 0.3 ft and 5:48 PM at 0.8 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of the 11:15 AM high in the sound.
waters.working: Waning gibbous at 88%, springs easing toward neap. The flood into the 11:15 high is the morning window - Coastal Angler's Topsail monthly, published Aug. 1 and a month old, has specks early on topwater before the bite fizzles mid-morning, redfish schools on spoons and soft plastics, and black drum on structure. Water 83.5F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast - and flounder opens tomorrow.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier runs well ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No watches, warnings or advisories posted for the Topsail area this morning per the National Weather Service.

kicker: Flounder opens on the coast at first light tomorrow; the Aki banzuke is out and every Tokyo session is sold.
